sensors.guide: The code must compile before the turn ends.
Run the unit tests before claiming done; fix the code, never the tests.
Checkstyle must pass; do not add suppressions without a reason.
Respect the layer rules in ArchitectureTest.

sensors.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d) && npx --yes jscpd@5.4.2 src/main --silent --reporters json --output "$d" >&2 && node -p "try{require('$d/jscpd-report.json').statistics.total.percentage}catch{0}"
sensors.guide: Reuse existing code instead of copying it; the duplicated share may not grow past its baseline.

sensors.cmd: if semgrep --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then semgrep scan --config p/default --error --metrics=off --disable-version-check --quiet {changed}; s=$?; [ $s -le 1 ] || [ -n "$CI" ] && exit $s; echo "sast: Semgrep could not scan here (exit $s: offline, or the rules did not load), so CI scans this change"; elif [ -n "$CI" ]; then echo 'sast: Semgrep does not run in CI (pipx install semgrep)'; exit 1; else echo 'sast: Semgrep does not run here (missing or broken), so CI scans this change (pipx install semgrep to scan locally)'; fi
sensors.guide: Semgrep scans the source files this change touches for security bugs (injection, unsafe input, secrets, weak crypto); fix the code rather than silencing the rule.
Do not add dependencies with known vulnerabilities.

sensors.cmd: S="${RIG_SDLC:-.rig/bin/sdlc.ts}"; [ -f "$S" ] || { echo 'mutation-diff: sdlc not found; re-run sdlc.ts vendor'; exit 1; }; mvn -v >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'mutation-diff: Maven is not installed: install Maven (the pitest plugin is fetched by the run), or the person waives mutation-diff'; exit 1; }; find . -path '*/target/pit-reports' -prune -exec rm -rf {} +; { mvn -q test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage -DtargetClasses="$(echo {changed:java} | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -E 's#.*src/main/(java|kotlin)/##; s#\.[a-z]+$#*#; s#/#.#g' | paste -sd, -)" -DoutputFormats=XML -DtimestampedReports=false -DfailWhenNoMutations=false || true; } >&2; node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "$S" mutscore --tool pitest --report $(find . -path '*/target/pit-reports/mutations.xml' | sort | tr '\n' ' ') --lines {changed-lines:java}; s=$?; find . -path '*/target/pit-reports' -prune -exec rm -rf {} +; exit $s
sensors.guide: Every line this change adds is pinned by a test: the mutation score on the changed lines must reach mutation.minScore; a survivor names a line and a change no test noticed, and goes back to the test writer. Needs pitest-maven (fetched by the run); JUnit 5 tests need the pitest-junit5-plugin as a plugin dependency in the pom. Multi-module builds write one report per module: all of them are read.
Tests must assert behaviour so that changing the code makes them fail.
